title: AMD and Anthropic Strike $5 Billion Chip Deal in Major AI Partnership
excerpt: Anthropic will deploy up to 2 gigawatts of AMD's next-generation MI450 GPUs, while AMD commits a strategic equity investment of up to $5 billion in the AI startup.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • AMD will invest up to $5 billion in Anthropic for AI infrastructure.
  • Anthropic will deploy 2 gigawatts of AMD MI450 GPUs starting in H1 2027.
  • The partnership positions AMD against Nvidia in the AI accelerator market.
  • AMD's revenue is projected to reach $82.2 billion in 2027.
  • The deal highlights a shift towards a multi-supplier AI hardware landscape.

A Landmark Deal in the AI Chip Race

Advanced Micro Devices and Anthropic on Tuesday announced what amounts to one of the largest AI infrastructure partnerships to date. Under the agreement, Anthropic will deploy up to 2 gigawatts of AMD's Instinct MI450 Series GPUs housed in AMD's Helios rack-scale solutions, with the first gigawatt beginning deployment in the first half of 2027.

AMD, for its part, has committed to a strategic equity investment of up to $5 billion in Anthropic, according to the official announcement and reporting by the Wall Street Journal and Reuters. The deal was announced on the eve of AMD's two-day "Advancing AI" conference in Santa Clara, where CEO Lisa Su is expected to showcase the company's growing roster of hyperscale AI customers.

"We are thrilled to deepen our partnership with Anthropic and deploy AMD Helios at gigawatt scale. This collaboration brings together Anthropic's leadership in frontier AI with the full strength of AMD high-performance computing."

— Dr. Lisa Su, Chair and CEO, AMD

Breaking Nvidia's Grip on AI Compute

The partnership positions AMD as a serious contender against Nvidia in the AI accelerator market. Anthropic becomes AMD's third gigawatt-level customer, joining Meta Platforms and OpenAI. GF Securities analyst Jeff Pu, who raised AMD's price target to $640 from $511, noted the Anthropic deployment scale is expected to exceed AMD's prior deals with Meta and OpenAI.

Anthropic will use AMD Helios rack-scale solutions featuring MI455X GPUs, together with AMD EPYC "Venice" CPUs, AMD Pensando networking, and ROCm software. The deployment builds on Anthropic's existing use of AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs. For Anthropic, the deal secures critical compute capacity to meet surging demand for its Claude AI models while diversifying its hardware supply chain.

"By partnering with AMD across the stack, we are securing the capacity we need and optimizing it for training and serving Claude," said Tom Brown, co-founder and chief compute officer at Anthropic. "Running across a diversified range of hardware lets us map the right workloads to the right hardware."

Engineering Collaboration and Software Push

Beyond hardware procurement, AMD and Anthropic are launching a multi-year engineering collaboration. The teams will use Claude to optimize workloads for AMD Instinct GPUs and accelerate development of AMD's ROCm software stack — a critical area where Nvidia's CUDA ecosystem has long maintained an advantage. AMD will also broadly adopt Claude across its engineering and product development teams.

The partnership comes as AMD reported a strong 2026, with GF Securities projecting full-year revenue of $52.3 billion for 2026 and $82.2 billion for 2027. AMD shares were up more than 4% on Monday ahead of the announcement, buoyed by a separate partnership expansion with Microsoft for Helios rack-scale solutions.

What This Means for the AI Industry

The AMD-Anthropic partnership signals a broader shift in the AI infrastructure landscape. The era of Nvidia's near-monopoly on AI training hardware is giving way to a multi-supplier environment where hyperscalers actively diversify their chip sources. For Indian-origin engineers and executives working across the semiconductor and AI sectors in Silicon Valley, this deal underscores the growing demand for AI infrastructure talent and the expanding career opportunities in the space.

AMD reports second-quarter financial results on August 4, with consensus estimates at $1.61 adjusted EPS on $11.3 billion in revenue. Investors will be watching Lisa Su's Advancing AI keynote on Thursday for further details on the Anthropic deployment timeline and additional customer announcements.
